## Overview

LRP200 is the **ability-adjusted** companion to [LRP100](../lrp-rli-mech-100/). It is the same
Tier-1 mechanism model — same exposure, outcome, own-baseline term, subject random
intercept and linear parameterisation — with `blocks` (WPPSI Block Design) added to the
matched conditioning set.

The Tier-1 negative-control panel found the letter-sound slope clearly positive on the
oral-language controls as well as the written-code outcomes, and named shared general
ability as the leading explanation for that non-specific component. Ability is latent and
structurally unblockable in the project's diagram, but a measured proxy exists: `blocks`
is complete, pre-treatment, and constant within child across all four waves. This variant
partials it out so the panel can be re-read with measured ability removed.

Role in the panel: **negative control** — the weakest oral-language control (18 items).

## Model

$$
\eta = \alpha + \alpha_{\text{phase}} + \beta_G G
  + \beta_{\text{mech}}\, z(\operatorname{logit}_* L_{\text{post}})
  + \gamma_{\text{own}}\operatorname{logit}_*(F_{\text{pre}})
  + \gamma_A z(A) + \gamma_{\text{blocks}} z(\text{blocks})
  + \sum_c \gamma_c z(c) + u_{\text{child}}.
$$

The added term relative to LRP100 is $\gamma_{\text{blocks}} z(\text{blocks})$.
`blocks` is a single noisy subtest rather than the latent ability node, so residual
confounding survives this adjustment and $\beta_{\text{mech}}$ remains an **adjusted
association**.
